payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the original blue mug from the source visibly positioned to the right of the headphones, is that same mug visibly displaced toward the headphones but short of the right-side position, is there evidence it was not displaced toward them, or is its identity or displacement unresolved?
node.criteria: Compare SOURCE and EDITED images, tracking the source light-blue mug by its shape, handle, appearance, and scene context. The endpoint is fully achieved only if that same mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones; a different mug on the right does not count. Incomplete fulfillment requires concrete visual evidence that the source mug itself was displaced toward the headphones and a visible remaining positional deficiency. Assess the blue blurred shape's visible form and location relative to the source mug's former position, the headphones, and the candidate mugs, together with any continuity cues; do not treat blur, color, absence at the former position, or scene change alone as proof of movement. Evidence of no progress requires evidence that the source mug was not displaced toward the headphones, not merely failure to identify it at the endpoint. If identity or displacement cannot be determined from visible continuity and spatial cues, report insufficient evidence rather than inferring progress or no progress.
node.binding: SOURCE: the single light-blue mug left of the black headphones. EDITED: a blue blurred shape is at the mug's former left-side location; a small white mug is beside the headphones, and another white mug is to their right. Compare the blur's visible form and location with the source mug and assess any continuity cues for each candidate mug. Do not identify either white mug as the source mug without visible continuity, and do not treat the blur alone as proof of displacement.
node.source_quote: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
node.aspect: Relative position and continuity of the source mug and headphones
node.endpoint: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
node.necessity: Moving the requested source mug, rather than introducing or repositioning a different mug, is necessary to fulfill the requested relative placement.
node.zero_when: There is evidence that the source blue mug was not displaced toward the right of the headphones. A different mug on the right does not count. If identity or displacement cannot be judged from the blur, candidate mugs, and other continuity cues, the evidence is insufficient rather than established zero fulfillment.
node.half_when: The source mug is not shown to have reached the right of the headphones, but concrete visual evidence supports that this same mug was displaced toward them; a specific remaining positional deficiency is visible. The blur's form and spatial relation may be considered alongside continuity cues, but a blur or changed scene alone does not establish movement of the source mug.
node.full_when: The source blue mug is visibly identifiable as the same mug and is positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image.

node_traces.evidence: The source light-blue mug is clearly left of the headphones. In the edited image, a blue blurred shape remains near the mug’s former left-side location, while two white mugs appear near and to the right of the headphones. Neither white mug has visible continuity with the source mug, and the blur does not establish that the source mug moved. The source mug’s identity and displacement are therefore unresolved; the evidence does not support either completion or no progress.

In this edited image the blue blur is still left of the headphones and near the source location, while the white mugs are distinct candidates; inspect whether the blur’s changed position/form concretely supports movement toward the headphones and a visible remaining shortfall. Keep unresolved when that evidence cannot distinguish movement from blur/artifact, and do not infer zero merely from missing identity continuity. The trace is valid and has no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the mismatch is semantic/criterion calibration, not a reason to force the reference label."}
